precisionGate: Review every finding up to 200; above 200, review every major cluster and a deterministic stratified sample of at least 50. Treat ambiguous findings as false positives for error-level rules.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews reproduced unanchored-banner and directive-prefix false positives, plus modern-HCL and block-comment false negatives. Fifty-eight focused cases and all 467 IaC tests pass. The repaired isolated corpus runner found zero diagnostics across 272 pinned tracked IaC/YAML files in Bulbul, Saqi, Automations, and Standards.
tasks.outcome: Kept the established no-comment-cruft ID, replaced broad substring and prefix matching with bounded forms, excluded generated/fixture and YAML scalar data, added conservative modern and balanced block-comment HCL coverage, improved paired public examples and messages, and collapsed disabled runs to one actionable diagnostic. Retain at error level.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews agreed the combined rule was not safe at error severity and reproduced false positives from omitted or nested-any types, JSON-backed declarations, backend/fixture files, inferred environment topology, and path-only caches. Eighty-six focused cases pass. A 23-file local tfvars corpus produced 286 advisory findings; the reviewers' stratified samples confirmed that cross-environment redundancy remains judgment-heavy.
tasks.outcome: Kept the shipped ID for selector and baseline compatibility, staged it as warning, rewrote certainty claims and public pairs, limited value comparison to fully declared scalar types, made unsupported or incomplete inputs abstain without tool-limitation diagnostics, excluded backend and fixture inputs, suppressed unsafe orphans when JSON declarations may exist, and removed stale path-only caches. A future major release should split provable orphan checks from advisory redundancy and explicit environment-inventory policy.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews agreed this is an organization-specific architecture preference rather than a universal Terraform error. They reproduced false positives for data-driven map selection, ambiguous workspace/stage/deployment names, malformed calls, and non-Terraform HCL, plus safe normalized-comparison misses. One hundred one focused cases pass. A 1,097-file local Terraform/Terragrunt scan produced 28 reviewed syntax matches, all within the intended advisory boundary, including security gates that still require human judgment.
tasks.outcome: Kept the shipped ID for compatibility, staged it as warning, rewrote categorical UI claims, allowed environment-keyed map lookup/index selection, restricted dialect scope, required literal evidence for ambiguous identity names, recognized bounded pure normalizers, enforced contains arity, excluded generated/fixture inputs, and made assertion exemptions structural. A future major release may rename it to no-environment-name-branching with executable selector aliases.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews kept the established name but found concrete false positives in YAML block scalars, fixture inputs, contiguous rationale comments, and plural headings over sibling declarations. Thirty-eight focused cases pass after repair. Local corpus reviews covered between 1,120 and 7,020 eligible files; the largest labeled review classified 40 of 43 matches as genuine and three grouping headings as false positives.
tasks.outcome: Kept the compatible no-restated-comment ID, staged it as warning, limited it to Terraform and Terragrunt HCL, excluded generated and fixture inputs, evaluated contiguous comment groups atomically, preserved sibling headings, recognized generic HCL blocks and common inflections, removed a broad security-word exemption, avoided overlap with commented-out HCL, and made public examples and diagnostics describe the actual declaration-level signal.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews rejected the categorical mock ban. HashiCorp documents empty mock providers as a supported credential-free configuration-testing mechanism, while the original matcher did not inspect assertions or data flow. The pinned local corpus contained one canonical match: an empty Google/PagerDuty mock used to assert configured plan values, a false positive under the rule's own rendered-plan allowance. Nineteen replacement cases pass.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ206 and its established selector for compatibility, staged it as warning, and replaced block-presence matching with run-scoped flow matching that reports only an assertion directly equating an override_resource, override_data, or override_module literal to the same target attribute. Empty mock providers, transformed assertions, provider-scoped overrides, JSON syntax, dynamic values, malformed HCL, and cross-run flows now abstain; public examples and remediation teach layered unit and provider-backed testing.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews found the safety objective useful but the error implementation provider-inaccurate: it accepted unsupported cross-provider attribute spellings, treated lifecycle.prevent_destroy as equivalent to provider protection, reported documented safe defaults as missing, and classified dynamic module inputs as proven unsafe. The pinned corpus had two actionable unguarded Cloud SQL child databases and one advisory variable-driven GKE guard. One hundred nineteen focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept the compatible require-deletion-protection ID, changed the category to correctness, staged it as warning, introduced exact resource-specific guard spellings, recognized documented protected-by-default Google resources and Cloud SQL API-side protection, rejected invalid quoted or case-incorrect booleans, limited parsing to maintained Terraform files, abstained on malformed inputs, and made each diagnostic recommend only valid controls while explaining that lifecycle protection disappears with the resource block.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews agreed resource type alone cannot prove irreplaceability and found a critical false negative: force_destroy = true silenced SARJ203 even though it enables contained-data deletion, including when the attribute was unsupported. The pinned corpus had eight useful but judgment-dependent unguarded Google Secret Manager leads and no force-destroy exemptions. Sixty-eight focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept the shipped selector for compatibility, changed the category to correctness, staged it as warning, replaced categorical irreplaceability claims with durable-data review language, made Google provider PREVENT the primary UI example, treated force_destroy/force_delete as destructive evidence instead of exemptions, required exact HCL booleans, restricted scope to maintained Terraform files, abstained on malformed inputs, and documented that lifecycle protection disappears when the resource block is removed.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews agreed the rule's name should remain stable but found that unlimited result sets, grouped and distinct queries, SQL in docstrings, and FETCH WITH TIES produced misleading findings, while volatile functions and constants were accepted as tie-break keys. Corpus review found 35 Bulbul and three AI findings with mixed impact, confirming this remains advisory without schema-level uniqueness evidence. Fifty-four focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept the established timestamp-order-requires-tiebreaker ID and alias, staged it as warning, limited findings to bounded row selection, excluded grouped, distinct, WITH TIES, generated, fixture, and docstring content, recognized static f-strings, rejected volatile or constant pseudo-keys, and rewrote examples and diagnostics to teach matching composite ORDER BY and keyset cursor predicates.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews agreed the local-explicitness policy is useful and has no Ruff or flake8-pytest-style equivalent. They reviewed 45 maintained local xfail calls: 38 literal-strict deterministic defect pins, six intentional nondeterministic or generated-case pins, and one non-defect environment marker. The rule emitted zero findings across a larger 83-repository, 6,634-file local Python sweep, so noise is low but live positive precision is not yet proven. One hundred focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ046, the established defect-xfail-requires-explicit-strict ID, and both aliases; staged it as warning; limited function findings to default-collected tests; excluded conftest, fixtures, generated code, nested helpers, and fully dynamic reasons; required literal strict=True; resolved Hypothesis and environment probes through imports; recognized statically false conditions and safe local xfail aliases; narrowed broad should prose to contrast statements; and rewrote UI copy to describe XPASS exit behavior and parameter-level remediation accurately.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews found 20 local diagnostics representing about 10 unique contexts, all policy-consistent, plus two genuine redundancies in a 529-file dependency sample. A broader pydantic-focused sample produced 87 deliberate structured API-table findings, proving the convention is unsuitable as a universal error. Reviewers also reproduced wrong deletion advice for stale documented names, docstring-only or mismatched types, swapped sibling descriptions, and aliased runtime decorators. Forty-seven focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ086 and the established docstring-args-restate-signature ID, staged it as warning, retained Google-style whole-block scope, mapped every entry to its actual parameter, compared only callable and matching-parameter name/type facts, preserved semantic qualifiers and mismatched or docstring-only types, exempted known aliased runtime decorators and overloads, named the callable in diagnostics, and replaced the misleading accepted UI example with a real unit-and-sentinel contract.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews classified 32 local findings clustered into 14 unique contexts: 13 were straightforward redundancies and one lost a boolean truth-condition contract. A 529-file dependency sample exposed two unannotated-function false positives, while a pydantic-heavy public API sample produced 91 intentional complete-table findings. Upstream tools own missing, extraneous, and mismatched result docs but not semantic restatement. Forty-six focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ087 and the established docstring-returns-restate-signature ID, staged it as warning, required one Google-style section and an informative explicit result annotation, compared only callable/class and the matching result slot, distinguished Generator yield and return slots, preserved input relationships, conditions, polarity, cardinality, ordering, identity, tuple roles, typed sections, overloads, and aliased runtime consumers, and rewrote UI guidance to remove only the redundant section.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews scanned between 7,097 and 7,477 Python files and reviewed 52 to 68 raw findings, with duplicated worktrees collapsing the independent set substantially. Many were useful parameterization prompts, but distinct liveness/readiness, authentication, card-action, privacy, and failure contracts were also reported. Four representative installed-package findings were plausible. Reviewers reproduced terminal-route and aliased pytest.raises match false positives. One hundred twenty-two focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ066, no-repeated-test-body, and its alias; staged it as warning; preserved every differing route literal as contract identity; resolved pytest.raises through import aliases; excluded conftest and methods on non-collected classes; narrowed external unittest inference to TestCase evidence; retained strong structural, fixture, prose, decorator, signature, and verbatim-copy guards; and rewrote UI claims from mandatory one-behavior parameterization to conditional consolidation or correction advice.

tasks.evidence: Three independent re-reviews found 48 to 54 local findings, all genuine cleaned-content copies on proven same-file bases, plus 14 representative dependency findings. Seven dependency findings were decorated methods whose direct runtime __doc__ could change. Reviewers reproduced a C3 diamond false positive, stale local bindings after imports or assignments, and meaningful formatting collapsed as equivalent. Thirty-two focused cases pass after repair.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ084, no-copied-inherited-docstring, and its alias; staged it as warning; limited resolution to one fully resolved local base; invalidated local base and alias bindings on imports and reassignment; abstained on multiple inheritance instead of guessing C3; excluded decorated methods; compared exact cleaned content without erasing internal formatting or punctuation; and rewrote UI guidance to disclose direct __doc__ behavior and preserve override-specific public documentation.

tasks.evidence: Three independent re-reviews classified 60 raw findings and 31 unique class ASTs across the local fleet: 21 had two or more direct test uses, two had one direct use, and eight were fixture- or helper-driven. Reviewers also found legitimate scenario-local doubles and confirmed that per-file analysis cannot prove cross-module reuse. A 772-file installed dependency sample produced zero findings.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ428 for compatibility as an explicitly advisory warning, not an error candidate. Reworded the UI to avoid asserting reuse, added Scripted coverage and a public scenario-local example, excluded non-collected support modules and non-infrastructure roots, and made support-directory recognition relative to a test root. A future repository-aware replacement should require cross-file import or structural-duplication evidence.

tasks.evidence: Three independent reviews ran 91 focused tests and classified a local fleet scan of 1,459 findings across 149 files: 625 parameter, 526 metadata, 263 alternate-response, 43 return, one routing, and one status finding. Roughly 80 percent were stricter organizational explicitness rather than broken generated OpenAPI. Reviewers reproduced false positives for concrete typed mappings, self-documenting non-JSON response classes, caught HTTPException calls, responses[*].model, and statically inherited APIRouter defaults and response maps.
tasks.outcome: Kept the compatible SARJ094 selector and alias but staged the composite rule as warning. Reworded its UI to distinguish FastAPI's valid inference from local explicitness policy, added a second public schema-integrity scenario, accepted concretely typed mappings and supported response models, inherited statically resolvable router response metadata, ignored caught exceptions and unverifiable custom response classes, and retained conservative direct-only analysis. Routing and other independently error-safe families remain candidates for future split rules after separate calibration.

tasks.evidence: Three independent re-reviews ran 56 focused tests and scanned 7,097 or more local Python files, finding 20 diagnostics across 19 paths. Every fleet finding reviewed was a record-like role bundle, but adversarial probes reproduced false positives for generator teardown return values, nested non-discoverable fixtures, rebound pytest imports, later type-alias rebinding, and explicitly homogeneous tuple sequences. Ruff has no equivalent fixture-result-shape rule; B901 owns generator return values instead.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ044, the accurate pytest-specific selector, and its compatibility alias; staged it as warning because a producer-only AST cannot distinguish every domain tuple protocol. Reworded the UI around unnamed positional records, upgraded the accepted UI flow to a frozen dataclass with typed consumers, made import and alias resolution lexical and rebinding-aware, limited fixtures to discoverable module or class scope, inspected only yielded values for generator fixtures, detected assigned yield expressions, unwrapped Annotated, exempted homogeneous and PEP 646 variadic tuple sequences, and aggregated branch results into one diagnostic per fixture.

tasks.evidence: Three independent re-reviews ran 29 focused tests and found five unique local candidates: four Bulbul stores with parallel ID-based SQL paths and one stateful AI computation-cache store. Adversarial probes showed that compatible annotations do not prove matching authorization, locking, transaction, replica, cache, conversion, or missing-row semantics; one live Bulbul singleton alone used prepare=False. The matcher also misclassified shared private helpers and multi-statement NotImplementedError stubs. Ruff and Pylint have no equivalent cross-method store-contract rule.
tasks.outcome: Kept SARJ421 and its compatibility alias, but staged the architectural inference as warning. Reworded the UI around equivalent observable semantics and concrete duplicated SQL, required Store-class and key-domain alignment, recognized shared private read helpers and multi-statement NotImplementedError stubs, and abstained on mismatched operational decorators, cache/authorization/transaction/replica signals, locking SQL, and behavior-affecting call keywords. Deliberately retained conservative method-name and type-shape boundaries.

tasks.evidence: Three independent re-reviews ran 30 focused tests and found three live diagnostics, all in Bulbul scripts/local_secrets/test_iac.py; each used Terraform substrings to infer project, IAM, conditional-binding, or deletion-protection behavior. Adversarial probes found ambiguity for golden and packaged representation contracts, false positives for tmp_path_factory outputs and suffix-changing Path calls, and misses for Path.open and decoded whole-file bytes. Ruff and Pylint have no equivalent oracle-dataflow rule.
tasks.outcome: Kept the cross-engine-compatible iac-source-coupled-test selector, clarified that Python currently targets Terraform/HCL behavior oracles, and staged SARJ412 as warning because exact representation contracts require judgment. Replaced the opaque plan example with a rendered-plan data assertion, documented exact suppression for golden or compatibility contracts, recognized Path.open, io.open, readlines, and decoded read_bytes flows, recomputed with_suffix and with_name source kinds, and treated tmp_path_factory and tmpdir_factory outputs as ephemeral.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 41 focused tests and scanned up to 2,959 tracked Python files across eight local repositories. The broadest scan found one live diagnostic, ai/python/shared/export_models.py:38, and runtime validation confirmed it is a true invalid NonEmptyStr default. An installed-source sample found five additional genuine non-null defaults. Two reviewers independently reproduced false positives where Pydantic before validators transform defaults during default validation; Ruff has no equivalent constraint-aware rule.
tasks.outcome: Kept invalid-pydantic-field-default and error severity after adding validator-aware abstention for exact field, model, root, and Annotated before/plain/wrap transformers. Clarified that direct assignments are covered, fixed the direct-None diagnostic, added a public nullability pair, recognized exact BaseModel plus Generic declarations, and expanded literal length checks to list, tuple, set, and dict defaults. Broader model inheritance, coercion inference, Pydantic v1, and dynamic constraints remain excluded to protect precision.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 53 focused tests and scanned up to 7,097 Python files. A primary-checkout scan produced 53 diagnostics across 14 files: many were useful repeated-construction clusters, while explicit expected records and full-contract calls confirmed the signal remains judgment-heavy. All reviewers reproduced false positives for disjoint keyword sets and generated tests; targeted probes also exposed pytest fixtures named test_*, import-resolved SimpleNamespace records, and unittest.mock.call expectations.
tasks.outcome: Kept repeated-kwarg-heavy-call-in-test and its compatibility alias, made SARJ045 explicitly warning-only, and required at least seven shared keyword names between calls to the same syntactic callee. Excluded generated files, exact pytest fixtures, import-resolved types.SimpleNamespace and unittest.mock.call data, and cross-class self/cls collisions. Reworked the public UI pair around incidental order setup, added parametrized-case remediation, and made diagnostics quantify keyword overlap and occurrences. Post-change calibration reported 47 warnings across 2,971 primary-checkout files, removing the demonstrated noise while preserving the reviewed high-value clusters.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 151 focused tests and scanned up to 7,097 Python files. Reviews found 360 to 638 diagnostics depending on tracked-primary versus all-checkout scope; stratified samples mixed genuine unrestricted collaborators with intentional leaf stubs and dynamic namespaces. All reviewers demonstrated that Mock(autospec=...), Mock(new=...), and Mock(new_callable=...) remain unrestricted despite being incorrectly accepted, and reproduced file-global shadowing, generated-source, patch DEFAULT/create, pytest-mocker inference, and post-construction mock_add_spec gaps. Ruff has no equivalent spec/autospec enforcement.
tasks.outcome: Kept mock-without-spec and made SARJ040 explicitly warning-only. Split constructor contracts from patcher controls; constructor autospec/new/new_callable attributes now report, while exact concrete patch replacements still abstain. Added provenance-aware DEFAULT handling, create=True or dynamic-create abstention, new_callable=None handling, generated-source exclusion, top-function-local shadowing, exact pytest test/fixture mocker inference, and pre-use mock_add_spec recognition. Reworked UI guidance to distinguish attribute specs from signature autospec and added a public patch pair. Post-change primary-checkout calibration reports 491 warnings across 2,971 Python files; unknown replacement factories and harder subscript-rooted stub analysis remain conservative.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 30 focused tests and scanned up to 13,930 Python files. Three paths represented two unique live findings: an endpoint-mount smoke test that accepts 404 and a named crash regression whose explicit contract is only avoiding HTTP 500. Reviewers reproduced false positives from terminal-name-only HTTPStatus/framework constants and nested or non-test-class test_* functions. Ruff and Pylint have no equivalent HTTP assertion-strength rule.
tasks.outcome: Kept negative-only-http-status-assertion for compatibility and made SARJ408 warning-only because intentional crash, fuzz, chaos, gateway, and smoke contracts require judgment. Added provenance-aware stdlib and FastAPI, Starlette, and Django REST Framework status constants, including import aliases; required an unshadowed builtin range; and limited analysis to module tests plus direct Test* or TestCase methods. UI remediation now permits a reasoned suppression for an intentional no-server-error contract, and the accepted example asserts the relevant payload. Post-change calibration retained the same two reviewed warnings across 2,971 primary-checkout files; broader alias and Boolean dataflow remain excluded.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 152 focused tests and scanned up to 13,930 Python files. They found 13 raw findings across eight files, including six already-suppressed bounded or transactional aggregates; only cache and task statistics were plausible analytics. All reviewers reproduced false positives for transactional SUM, scheduler MIN, version MAX, bounded DISTINCT and JSON aggregation, SQLite or MySQL stores, and executable-looking SQL in docstrings. File-wide ClickHouse and BigQuery exclusions also hid PostgreSQL queries in mixed-backend modules. Ruff, Pylint, and SQLFluff do not own this datastore-placement policy.
tasks.outcome: Kept no-analytical-aggregation-in-postgres-store for selector compatibility and made SARJ020 explicitly warning-only. The rule now requires positive PostgreSQL ownership evidence and reports only statistical aggregates or time-bucketed grouped rollups; ordinary operational aggregates and mutations intentionally abstain. Added generated-source and AST-docstring exclusions, replaced provider-wide exemptions with per-query ClickHouse and BigQuery syntax classification, rewrote the UI pair around an unmistakable reporting rollup versus a bounded transactional invariant, and made the diagnostic request bounds and execution-plan review rather than unconditional offload. Post-change calibration produced zero warnings across 2,757 Bulbul and AI Python files while retaining focused synthetic coverage for newly introduced reporting scans.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository token/AST calibration produced 59 findings. Category and targeted-context review confirmed untracked work, decorative section boundaries, mechanical narration, and one statement walkthrough; protected rationales, tracked work, directives, docstrings, and generated code remained clean.
tasks.outcome: Kept the concise umbrella name, made the summary enumerate the actual policy, tightened banner guidance around named code boundaries, and broadened untracked-work detection from TODO/FIXME to HACK/XXX/BUG. These human work markers are no longer misclassified as machine directives and become valid when linked to a ticket or context URL.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Targeted adversarial cases established the missed import forms while preserving support-module, pytest API, and non-conftest imports.
tasks.outcome: Kept the precise rule name, expanded analysis beyond top-level imports, detected `from tests import test_api` and relative equivalents without treating helper symbols as modules, and added literal pytest_plugins coverage. Dynamically assembled plugin paths remain outside the deterministic boundary.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Targeted mutation cases demonstrated deterministic duplicates that the prior declaration-only analysis missed, while dynamic values and destructive or opaque mutations remained excluded.
tasks.outcome: Kept the exact rule name and extended the static contract through literal __all__.append, extend, and insert operations, reporting the later duplicate at its mutation argument and preserving the original declaration line in the diagnostic.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Targeted flow cases proved router, alias, annotation, and rebinding behavior without inferring factory-returned applications or dynamic event names.
tasks.outcome: Kept the recognizable FastAPI-centered ID, added APIRouter and Starlette Router contracts, propagated simple application and `.router` aliases, recognized annotated bindings, and made provenance flow-sensitive so a later unrelated rebinding removes the diagnostic.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository token calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Pinned Ruff probes confirmed that exact `ruff: noqa: TID251`, `ruff: file-ignore[TID251]`, and the preferred `ruff: file-ignore[banned-api]` suppress the protected rule, while selector prefixes, `ALL`, and colon-style file-ignore lookalikes are invalid.
tasks.outcome: Renamed the rule around file-level suppression rather than legacy noqa syntax, added Ruff's modern name-based file-ignore form, and kept inline suppressions, mechanical rules, invalid lookalikes, and balanced disable/enable ranges outside the diagnostic boundary. The public example now teaches Ruff's canonical modern spelling.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration found 45 private first-party imports, all in white-box tests directly coupled to production internals; the other two corpora were clean. Review retained all 45 under the explicit consumer-boundary policy. Literal dynamic-import broadening added no corpus findings, and targeted rebinding cases established the conservative provenance boundary.
tasks.outcome: Kept the accurate first-party-private-import ID, corrected the summary and remediation to include white-box tests, moved the public example to a production package consumer, and added literal `importlib.import_module` detection for private first-party modules. Only stable stdlib import provenance is accepted; aliases that are rebound, dynamic strings, relative dynamic imports, and third-party loaders remain excluded.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Current official Pydantic documentation confirms that model configuration may use ConfigDict, a plain dictionary, or BaseModel class arguments; targeted tests cover all three frozen forms plus conflicting and dynamic configuration exclusions.
tasks.outcome: Kept the technically exact rule name and added the two documented frozen-model declarations the prior implementation missed: literal model_config dictionaries and `frozen=True` class arguments. Conflicting configuration channels, unpacked or computed dictionaries, inherited config, and ambiguous multiple inheritance remain excluded rather than guessing Pydantic's effective merge semantics.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository embedded-SQL calibration produced zero findings after broadening. Targeted adversarial cases exposed the prior literal-wide UUIDv7 exemption: a separate uuidv7 call or builder expression could hide an unrelated gen_random_uuid call in the same string. Per-occurrence nesting retains legitimate compatibility builders while reporting the unrelated random UUID.
tasks.outcome: Renamed the rule around its actual random-UUID premise, retained the old hook ID as an alias, added uuid-ossp `uuid_generate_v4()`, and replaced global compatibility heuristics with per-call enclosing-function analysis. UUIDv7 remains the explicit required replacement; genuine UUIDv7 compatibility function definitions stay exempt.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST calibration produced zero findings before and after broadening. Targeted overload cases demonstrated that counting declarations rather than exported names let one-responsibility utility modules escape, while the expanded exact-stem corpus remained clean.
tasks.outcome: Kept the precise responsibility-oriented name, expanded the junk-drawer set with the exact `utility` and `utilities` stems, and now counts distinct public definition names so overload declarations remain one export. Constants, type aliases, explicit __all__ surfaces, generated sources, tests, framework conventions, and near-miss stems retain their conservative exemptions.

tasks.evidence: Three-repository AST and cross-file calibration produced one finding: a consumer JWT service constructor with four optional arguments falling back to application settings. Review confirmed the full finding as a hidden composition dependency. Broadening retained that single corpus result while targeted cases covered missed positional and direct-field branch forms.
tasks.outcome: Kept the precise rule name and its strong settings-provider plus first-party-construction gates. Expanded optional-parameter detection from keyword-only arguments to positional-only and positional-or-keyword defaults, and recognized `if option is None: self.option = settings.VALUE` without treating assignments to unrelated fields as the option's fallback.

tasks.evidence: Final fleet calibration scanned 6,635 tracked Python files across 36 local projects with zero analyzer issues. All 94 remaining findings were inspected true direct psycopg pool access outside a support boundary; earlier shared-support and setup/cleanup fixture false positives drove explicit exemptions. Focused behavior coverage passed 12 of 12 cases.
tasks.outcome: Kept provenance-aware SARJ429 at warning level with lexical function scoping, explicit pool-type proof, shared test-support and conftest exemptions, and fixture-internal setup/cleanup handling. Fixtures that expose a raw connection and ordinary tests/helpers remain reportable; promotion requires a clean adoption window.

tasks.evidence: Fleet calibration scanned 6,636 tracked Python files across 36 local projects. Both findings were inspected fresh adjacent dict builders whose comprehensions preserve observable behavior: two true positives and zero false positives. Focused behavior and performance gates remain clean.
tasks.outcome: Added warning-stage SARJ430 only for derived dict projections, destructured list projections, and filtered set builders that Ruff PERF401, PERF403, and FURB142 miss. Fresh adjacent initialization, callable scope, liveness, simple projection, comment, control-flow, and 120-column gates keep the preference narrow. No autofix is offered because dict assignment and comprehension key/value evaluation order can differ.

tasks.evidence: Fleet calibration scanned 6,636 tracked Python files across 36 local projects and inspected all seven findings. Every match was a boolean-only intersection between locally proven built-in sets: seven true positives and zero false positives.
tasks.outcome: Staged at warning without autofix. The rule excludes unproven operands and stored intersections because short-circuiting can expose equality/hash side effects; promotion requires a clean adoption window.

tasks.evidence: Twenty adversarial passes narrowed the rule to physically adjacent one-line awaited calls and one-return None guards. A 7,516-file corpus found 62 exact-boundary candidates after excluding 48 blank-gap cases; the primary application target and all nine current findings were manually accepted.
tasks.outcome: Required same-indentation physical adjacency, token-aware comment preservation, a 120-column combined condition, later same-scope use before rebinding, and no else or autofix; staged the style rule as a warning.

tasks.evidence: Three application repositories scanned: 3 findings reviewed, 3 trigger-backed application behaviors, 0 false positives; two repositories had no findings.
tasks.outcome: Renamed and broadened SARJ114 to cover trigger creation and re-enablement while allowing DROP and DISABLE operations; exact suppressions document approved database-owned invariants.

tasks.evidence: Fleet calibration scanned 1,325 tracked operational files across 118 local checkouts representing 103 projects. After separating application publication from infrastructure ownership, all 28 remaining diagnostics were reviewed true control-plane mutations and zero were false positives; 24 Wrangler and 35 Cloud Run application publishes were independently verified as accepted near misses.
tasks.outcome: Staged the corrected rule at warning level with one finding per file, command-aware shell parsing, structured workflow run scalars and deployment Actions, operational JSON coverage, and explicit application-publish handling for Wrangler and artifact-only Cloud Run releases. Resource lifecycle, IAM, configuration, secrets, Kubernetes mutation, and plan-address allowlists remain reported; promotion requires a later clean adoption window.

tasks.evidence: Re-running `code-standards --root ROOT maintain rules evaluate --rule text:workflow-embedded-program --scope corpus .github/workflows` on the three pinned local workflow trees produced 98 diagnostics: 15 in the public Standards tree and 83 in two private trees. Every location was inspected with zero known false positives; small inline probes and shell guards remain intentionally warning-only. Three sequential warm runs had a 0.30 second median on the public tree and 0.41 second median on the largest private tree. The labeled suite adds numeric, dashed, dynamic-looking, tab-stripped, escaped, and multiple heredocs; YAML aliases; shell-keyword executable paths; here-strings; and combined or attached interpreter flags.
tasks.outcome: Staged SARJ310 at warning with direct-workflow path scoping, YAML scalar parsing, quote/comment state, a queued shell-word heredoc scanner, YAML-alias deduplication, literal control-keyword matching, combined interpreter inline-source flags, one diagnostic per run scalar, and SARJ309 precedence that respects rule selection. Multiline jq, data heredocs, external interpreter scripts, nested workflow-like YAML, reusable Actions, direct repository commands, and ordinary multiline orchestration remain clean. Workflow topology, ownership, redundancy, long linear command lists, wrapper-indirected behavior, and unrecognized interpreter languages remain explicit review boundaries rather than inferred findings.

tasks.evidence: Type-aware fleet calibration scanned 12,913 tracked JavaScript and TypeScript files across 58 local projects, then exhaustively evaluated all 368 filter(Boolean) candidate files. All 13 findings preserved runtime filtering and improved narrowing: 13 true positives and zero false positives.
tasks.outcome: Staged at warning with an explicit editor suggestion using value !== null && value !== undefined. Broad primitives, falsy literals, custom filters, shadowed Boolean, any, unknown, generics, and untyped runs remain excluded; promotion requires a clean adoption window.

tasks.evidence: Fleet calibration scanned 6,636 present tracked Python files across 83 local checkouts with zero findings; one absent tracked file was recorded as incomplete coverage. Immutable public calibration scanned 4,506 FastAPI, Pydantic, and Django files with zero findings, while the cited PR 5401 activation helper produced exactly one finding.
tasks.outcome: Narrowed the warning from lexical comment density to a long paragraph immediately preceding an empty local collection followed by at least two adjacent accumulator calls. Ordinary rationale comments and multiple extend calls without narration remain accepted.

tasks.evidence: Safe config-independent fleet calibration parsed 13,290 present tracked JavaScript and TypeScript files across 61 local checkouts with zero parser failures and one reviewed true positive; six absent tracked files were recorded as incomplete coverage. Immutable public calibration scanned 1,105 Zod, Hono, and Axios files with zero findings, while the cited PR 5401 adapter and API-contract headers produced exactly two findings.
tasks.outcome: Narrowed the warning to oversized unattached file-header JSDoc that narrates module layout or change history. Durable protocol, runtime, algorithm, and declaration documentation remains accepted.

tasks.evidence: Five-agent design review plus a 33-codebase syntax-aware corpus study parsed 957 unique Zod-bearing files without failures and proved 3,951 handwritten production schema bindings.
